rows.body: Curio Collection by Hilton standards vary by conversion path, F&B program, and agreement vintage. Use the table as a planning checklist—confirm every row in the FDD, design manual, and LOI before capital commitments.

rows.title: Breakfast / Morning Meal
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Restaurant-forward F&B or brand-approved morning offering—not complimentary F&B-led limited-service.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm kitchen, restaurant concept, staffing, and food cost model.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: F&B program is core to lifestyle positioning.

rows.title: Lobby / Public Space
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Design-forward arrival, social spaces, and local rituals touchpoints.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm layout, FF&E, and conversion flexibility for neighborhood character.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Lifestyle collection requires higher design investment than select-service.

rows.title: Guestroom Standards
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Design-forward bedding, bath, finishes, and FF&E per Curio standards.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm PIP scope, procurement, and room mix.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Conversions often need project-specific design review.

rows.title: Fitness / Pool
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Fitness and/or pool where market and prototype require.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm minimum size, equipment, and operating cost.
Typical status: May Apply

rows.title: Signage / Exterior
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Curio signage and exterior identity within Hilton portfolio.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm monument, façade, historic preservation, and permitting.
Typical status: Typically Expected

rows.title: Technology / Systems
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Hilton PMS, CRS, Hilton Honors, Wi-Fi, and reporting integrations.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm cutover timeline, training, and recurring tech fees.
Typical status: Typically Expected

rows.title: Training / QA

Typical status: Typically Expected

rows.title: Nacar Hotel Cartagena, Curio Collection by Hilton
rows.body:
Urban, Colombia, CALA, Walled City, Lifestyle boutique

Cartagena, Colombia (Centro Histórico / Walled City)

Historic conversion · lifestyle boutique · restaurant-forward urban

Nacar Hotel Cartagena is a Curio Collection property in Cartagena's walled historic center—design-led rooms, rooftop pool, and courtyard public spaces positioned for leisure and regional transient demand in Colombia's primary coastal heritage market.

Compare this format if you are underwriting a colonial-core lifestyle conversion in CALA: authentic public spaces, F&B complexity, and design PIP—not select-service reflag economics.

Walled-city Curio assets need operator F&B discipline and design QA matched to local ADR—confirm Hilton fees, incentives, and conversion scope before you model from U.S. gateway prototypes.

https://www.hilton.com/en/hotels/ctgncqq-nacar-hotel-cartagena/

rows.title: Zemi Miches Punta Cana All-Inclusive Resort, Curio Collection by Hilton
rows.body:
Resort, Dominican Republic, CALA, All-inclusive, Beachfront

Miches, Dominican Republic (Playa Esmeralda / northeast coast)

All-inclusive resort · 500 keys · multi-venue F&B and pools

Zemi Miches is Curio Collection's first all-inclusive resort in the Dominican Republic—a large-format beachfront property on Playa Esmeralda with multiple restaurants, pools, spa, and Club Azure premium tier. Distinct operating model from à la carte Curio urban or boutique formats.

If you are evaluating all-inclusive Curio, underwrite on AI package economics, F&B outlet count, and labor intensity—not urban collection or small boutique PIP assumptions.

Large AI resorts swing on occupancy and package margin—confirm Hilton program fees, AI operator capability, and air-lift leisure mix before you model from urban Curio comps.

https://www.hilton.com/en/hotels/pujmiqq-zemi-miches-all-inclusive-resort/

rows.title: Royal Palm Galapagos, Curio Collection by Hilton
rows.body:
Resort, Ecuador, CALA, Galápagos, Nature destination lodge

Santa Cruz Island, Galápagos, Ecuador (highland forest estate)

Nature lodge · low density · villas and suites · eco-sensitive destination

Royal Palm Galapagos is a Curio Collection estate on Santa Cruz Island—21 villas and deluxe rooms on a 160-hectare highland property adjacent to Galápagos National Park, positioned for ultra-nature leisure and expedition-style demand.

Destination-lodge Curio is a distinct underwriting profile: low key count, high experience capex, strict environmental constraints, and logistics-heavy operations—not beach AI or urban collection templates.

Galápagos assets require realistic transfer, permitting, and shoulder-season assumptions—confirm operator eco-compliance and Hilton program economics before you borrow from mainland resort comps.

Upper-upscale soft collection within Hilton—individually remarkable hotels with distinctive architecture, culinary-forward F&B, and destination-native experiences—not select-service, extended-stay, or rigid chain retail.

Upper-upscale soft collection within Hilton—Curio sits with Tapestry as the independent-character tier; below Waldorf Astoria, Conrad, and LXR luxury; above Hilton Hotels & Resorts core full-service, DoubleTree, and Garden Inn—not Hampton, Tru, Spark, or Homewood extended-stay formats.

Conversion and repositioning of independent and soft-brand full-service assets across urban, resort, and experiential destinations; selective new-build and adaptive reuse. FDD paths include New Development, Conversion, Change of Ownership, and Re-licensing—confirm pipeline and incentives with Hilton development.

Independent and soft-brand full-service conversions where the asset already has story, F&B complexity, and local character—Curio adds Hilton Honors and distribution without erasing individuality.

Destination resort and experiential repositioning—beach, golf, nature lodge, or all-inclusive formats where authenticity and culinary moments justify upper-upscale ADR with Hilton's revenue engine.

Adaptive reuse and heritage repositioning—historic urban, landmark, or architecturally distinctive buildings where conversion PIP and design narrative unlock premium positioning versus select-service reflag economics.

rows.title: Independent & Soft-Brand Conversion
rows.body: Full-service independent or soft-brand assets with existing story and F&B complexity—Curio retains local character while adding Hilton Honors, global sales, supply management, and distribution. Best when the building can support upper-upscale full-service economics, not limited-service reflag.

rows.title: Destination Resort & Experiential Repositioning
rows.body: Resorts, beach, golf, nature lodges, and all-inclusive properties where destination authenticity and culinary experiences drive ADR—Curio's flexible brand standards accommodate format diversity (à la carte urban to large-format AI) while connecting to Hilton's loyalty and commercial stack.

rows.title: Adaptive Reuse & Heritage Repositioning
rows.body: Historic urban cores, walled cities, landmark buildings, and adaptive reuse where architecture and sense of place are the product—conversion PIP and design narrative unlock premium positioning. Confirm Hilton fees, incentives, and heritage constraints before modeling from U.S. gateway prototypes.

Keep your independent spirit—just add Hilton: retain hotel individuality and local character while accessing Hilton Honors, global sales, Hilton Supply Management, and revenue systems.
Remarkable characters: hand-picked upper-upscale hotels in sought-after urban and resort destinations—198 open across 47 countries (May 2026 fact sheet).
Culinary-forward positioning: world-class F&B from beachfront cocktails to chef-driven tasting menus—not generic hotel dining.
Conversion-friendly economics: FDD supports conversion, adaptive reuse, and new development—model ~75% avg Hilton Honors occupancy contribution from your Item 19 sample (2025 U.S. comparable hotels).
